name: Cognitive Behavioral Therapy for Depression
description: Evidence-based Cognitive Behavioral Therapy protocol designed to help identify and modify negative thought patterns and behaviors contributing to depression. This structured 12-week program combines behavioral activation, cognitive restructuring, and relapse prevention.
contraindications: Active suicidal ideation requiring immediate intervention
Severe substance use disorder (requires concurrent treatment)

goals: Understand the CBT model of depression
Learn relationship between thoughts, emotions, and behaviors
Complete baseline assessment and symptom tracking
interventions: Psychoeducation on Depression and CBT Model

goals: Challenge cognitive distortions and automatic negative thoughts
Execute behavioral experiments to test assumptions
Consolidate therapeutic gains and symptom reduction
Formulate personalized relapse prevention and early-warning plan

milestones.description: Baseline to week 4 PHQ-9 reduction of 20%
Consistent use of at least 3 CBT skills
PHQ-9 score in minimal or mild range

references: Beck, A.T., Rush, A.J., Shaw, B.F., & Emery, G. (1979). Cognitive Therapy of Depression. Guilford Press.
Greenberger, D., & Padesky, C.A. (2015). Mind Over Mood, Second Edition. Guilford Press.
Wright, J.H., Brown, G.K., Thase, M.E., & Basco, M.R. (2017). Learning Cognitive-Behavior Therapy, Second Edition. American Psychiatric Publishing.
Cuijpers, P., et al. (2013). A meta-analysis of cognitive-behavioural therapy for adult depression. Journal of Affective Disorders, 142(1-3), 27-35.

weeklyCurriculum.title: Understanding Depression and CBT
goals: Learn about the connection between thoughts, feelings, and behaviors
objectives: Identify personal depression symptoms and patterns

exercises.name: CBT Model Introduction
exercises.description: Learn how thoughts, feelings, and behaviors are interconnected in depression
exercises.instructions: Review the CBT model diagram. Write down one recent situation where you felt down and identify the thoughts, feelings, and behaviors involved.

exercises.name: Depression Symptom Tracking
exercises.description: Begin tracking your daily mood and activities
exercises.instructions: Rate your mood 3 times daily (morning, afternoon, evening) on a scale of 0-10. Note any activities you engaged in.

exercises.name: Goal Setting Worksheet
exercises.description: Set specific, measurable goals for therapy
exercises.instructions: Write down 3 goals you want to achieve through this program. Make them SMART (Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant, Time-bound).

checkpoints: Has set at least 2 therapy goals

weeklyCurriculum.title: Activity Scheduling and Pleasure
goals: Break the cycle of withdrawal and isolation
objectives: Distinguish between necessary and pleasurable activities

exercises.name: Activity-Mood Connection
exercises.description: Track activities and their impact on your mood
exercises.instructions: For each activity, rate your mood before (0-10) and after (0-10). Notice patterns in what activities improve your mood.

exercises.name: Pleasant Activities Inventory
exercises.description: Create a list of activities you used to enjoy or want to try
exercises.instructions: List 20 activities across categories: social, physical, creative, learning, self-care, outdoor. Rate each for feasibility (1-5).

exercises.name: Weekly Activity Schedule
exercises.description: Schedule pleasant activities into your week
exercises.instructions: Choose 5-7 activities from your inventory. Schedule specific times for each. Start small and build gradually.

homeworkAssignments: Complete at least 3 scheduled pleasant activities
Notice which activities most improve mood
checkpoints: Has scheduled activities for the week

weeklyCurriculum.title: Overcoming Avoidance and Building Routines
objectives: Use gradual exposure to overcome avoidance

exercises.name: Avoidance Identification
exercises.description: Identify tasks and situations you've been avoiding
exercises.instructions: List 5-10 things you've been avoiding. For each, rate difficulty (1-10) and importance (1-10). Start with easiest/most important.

exercises.name: Graded Task Assignment
exercises.description: Break down avoided tasks into manageable steps
exercises.instructions: Choose one avoided task. Break it into 5-7 small steps. Complete the first step this week.

exercises.name: Daily Routine Builder
exercises.description: Create a consistent daily routine structure
exercises.instructions: Design a daily routine with consistent wake/sleep times, meals, activities. Include both pleasant and necessary activities.

homeworkAssignments: Complete first step of graded task
checkpoints: Has begun addressing one avoided task

weeklyCurriculum.title: Identifying Negative Automatic Thoughts
goals: Recognize common thinking patterns in depression
Begin connecting thoughts to mood changes

exercises.name: Automatic Thought Introduction
exercises.description: Learn about automatic thoughts and their role in depression
exercises.instructions: Review examples of automatic thoughts. Practice catching your own thoughts when mood shifts.

exercises.name: Simple Thought Record
exercises.description: Track situations, thoughts, and feelings
exercises.instructions: When you notice mood change: (1) Describe situation, (2) Identify thought, (3) Name emotion and rate intensity (0-100).

exercises.name: Cognitive Distortions Checklist
exercises.description: Learn common thinking errors in depression
exercises.instructions: Review 10 common cognitive distortions. Identify which ones you use most frequently. Find examples from your thought records.

homeworkAssignments: Identify cognitive distortions in your thinking

weeklyCurriculum.title: Challenging and Modifying Negative Thoughts
goals: Learn to challenge negative automatic thoughts
Experience mood improvement through cognitive change
objectives: Use evidence-based questioning to challenge thoughts

exercises.name: Socratic Questioning
exercises.description: Learn to question and evaluate your thoughts
exercises.instructions: For negative thoughts, ask: What's the evidence? Are there alternative explanations? What would I tell a friend? What's the worst/best/most realistic outcome?

exercises.name: 7-Column Thought Record
exercises.description: Complete thought record with evidence and alternatives
exercises.instructions: Use full thought record: situation, thoughts, emotions, evidence for/against, alternative thought, re-rate emotion.

exercises.name: Alternative Thought Practice
exercises.description: Generate balanced alternative thoughts
exercises.instructions: For each negative thought from this week, write 2-3 alternative balanced thoughts. Rate believability of each (0-100).

homeworkAssignments: Practice Socratic questioning on negative thoughts
Notice mood changes after cognitive restructuring
checkpoints: Reports some mood improvement from restructuring

weeklyCurriculum.title: Identifying and Understanding Core Beliefs
goals: Understand the concept of core beliefs
Recognize how core beliefs influence automatic thoughts
objectives: Distinguish between automatic thoughts and core beliefs
Begin exploring evidence for/against core beliefs

exercises.name: Core Beliefs Introduction
exercises.description: Learn about core beliefs and their role in depression
exercises.instructions: Review the three levels: core beliefs → intermediate beliefs → automatic thoughts. Understand how they're connected.

exercises.name: Downward Arrow Technique
exercises.description: Uncover core beliefs underlying automatic thoughts
exercises.instructions: Choose a strong negative thought. Ask 'What does that mean about me?' repeatedly until you reach a core belief.

exercises.name: Core Belief Identification
exercises.description: Identify your primary core beliefs
exercises.instructions: Review your thought records for themes. Common themes often reveal core beliefs. Rate strength of each belief (0-100).

homeworkAssignments: Continue thought records focusing on belief themes
checkpoints: Can connect automatic thoughts to core beliefs

weeklyCurriculum.title: Structured Problem Solving Skills

exercises.name: Problem-Solving Model
exercises.description: Learn the 5-step problem-solving approach
exercises.instructions: Review the 5 steps: (1) Define problem, (2) Brainstorm solutions, (3) Evaluate options, (4) Choose and implement, (5) Review outcome.

exercises.name: Current Problems List
exercises.description: Identify and prioritize current problems
exercises.instructions: List all current problems. Rate each for: controllability (1-5), importance (1-5), urgency (1-5). Choose one to work on.

exercises.name: Problem-Solving Worksheet
exercises.description: Apply structured problem-solving to chosen problem
exercises.instructions: Follow 5-step model for your chosen problem. Generate at least 5 possible solutions. Choose best option and create action plan.

homeworkAssignments: Apply problem-solving to one new problem
checkpoints: Has implemented at least one solution

weeklyCurriculum.title: Improving Social Connections and Communication

exercises.name: Social Network Mapping
exercises.description: Assess current social connections and identify gaps
exercises.instructions: Create a map of current relationships. Identify supportive people, neutral people, draining relationships. Note desired changes.

exercises.name: Assertiveness Training
exercises.description: Learn and practice assertive communication
exercises.instructions: Review passive, aggressive, and assertive styles. Practice 'I' statements. Role-play common scenarios.

exercises.name: Social Activity Planning
exercises.description: Schedule social activities for the week
exercises.instructions: Plan 2-3 social activities (in-person or virtual). Start small: coffee with friend, family dinner, online group.

homeworkAssignments: Reach out to one person from support network

weeklyCurriculum.title: Integrating CBT Skills
objectives: Identify personal "tool kit" of most effective strategies
Apply multiple techniques to current situations
Build confidence in using skills independently

exercises.name: CBT Skills Review
exercises.description: Review all techniques learned in weeks 1-8
exercises.instructions: List all skills learned: behavioral activation, thought records, core beliefs, problem-solving, social skills. Rate helpfulness (1-10).

exercises.name: Personal Coping Card
exercises.description: Create a personalized quick reference guide
exercises.instructions: On a card, write: (1) Your top 5 most helpful skills, (2) Warning signs of depression return, (3) Emergency contacts.

exercises.name: Case Formulation
exercises.description: Create your personal CBT case formulation
exercises.instructions: Map out: your core beliefs → intermediate beliefs → automatic thoughts → behaviors → consequences. Identify vicious cycles.

homeworkAssignments: Use at least 3 different CBT skills this week
Notice which skills work best in which situations
checkpoints: Can identify personal most effective skills

weeklyCurriculum.title: Recognizing Warning Signs and Triggers
objectives: List early warning signs of depression return

exercises.name: Warning Signs Identification
exercises.description: Identify your personal depression warning signs
exercises.instructions: Reflect on past depressive episodes. List: first signs, early symptoms, behavioral changes. Rate how early each sign appears.

exercises.name: Triggers and High-Risk Situations
exercises.description: Identify situations that increase depression risk
exercises.instructions: List: stressful life events, seasonal patterns, relationship issues, work stress, sleep disruption. Rate risk level for each.

exercises.name: Early Intervention Plan
exercises.description: Create action plan for early warning signs
exercises.instructions: For each warning sign, specify: (1) CBT skills to use, (2) Who to contact, (3) Activities to increase, (4) When to seek help.

homeworkAssignments: Review and refine early intervention plan
Practice implementing plan for minor mood dip

weeklyCurriculum.title: Maintaining Gains and Building Resilience
objectives: Identify factors that contributed to improvement
Create maintenance schedule for CBT skills

exercises.name: Progress Review
exercises.description: Assess changes since beginning of program
exercises.instructions: Compare current PHQ-9 to baseline. List: symptoms improved, skills mastered, goals achieved, areas still challenging.

exercises.name: Resilience Building
exercises.description: Learn strategies for long-term mental health
exercises.instructions: Review resilience factors: social support, self-care, meaning/purpose, healthy lifestyle. Rate current level of each (1-10).

exercises.name: Maintenance Plan
exercises.description: Create ongoing practice schedule
exercises.instructions: Schedule: weekly thought records, monthly goal review, ongoing behavioral activation, regular social activities. Set calendar reminders.

checkpoints: Demonstrates confidence in managing future challenges

weeklyCurriculum.title: Program Completion and Moving Forward
objectives: Plan for ongoing support if needed

exercises.name: Program Review
exercises.description: Comprehensive review of 12-week program
exercises.instructions: Review each week's focus. Note key learnings, most helpful exercises, breakthrough moments. Create personal highlights list.

exercises.name: Relapse Prevention Final Plan
exercises.description: Finalize comprehensive relapse prevention strategy
exercises.instructions: Combine: warning signs, triggers, early intervention plan, maintenance schedule, support contacts, when to seek help.

exercises.name: Letter to Future Self
exercises.description: Write letter to read during future challenges
exercises.instructions: Write to yourself: What you've learned, how far you've come, what helps, encouragement for tough times. Seal and save.

homeworkAssignments: Review letter to future self in 3 months
